session.title: Codex capacity 429s and WSL-renewed logins fixed (1.0.46); sign in without switching (1.0.47); user-b.zhang signed back in
session.purpose: the user asked what happened to the second GPT account (user-b.zhang). The investigation found two Switchy bugs (capacity 429s bouncing requests between accounts; a Codex login renewed in WSL lost), which he had fixed, built, installed and released as 1.0.46. He then asked for a way to sign an account in without moving programs off their account, exposed as control routes an agent drives; built and released as 1.0.47 and used to sign user-b.zhang back in.
outcomes: Diagnosed user-b.zhang (f7649e3f) signed out 2026-10-25 20:06 with 'refresh token has already been used': its stored login dated from 2026-10-16; Codex renews at 8 days, Switchy then renewed only 5 min before the 10-day expiry; a plain Codex in WSL renewing a non-current account wrote only WSL's auth.json, which Switchy never read and overwrote at the next switch. Claude got the same fix on 2026-10-09; Codex had not. The account was at 100% of its week from 08:10 (week started 2026-10-24 23:10, used up in about 9 h).

Diagnosed 358 Codex switches 2026-10-25 08:32-09:53: OpenAI answered registered2nd with 429 turn_rate_limit_exceeded ('Codex is at capacity'); Switchy counted any 429 as a usage limit, held the account out 5 min and resent each turn to user-b.zhang (really at its limit) and back with no cap. Codex transcripts show no terminal saw the capacity message during the bursts; a 503 server_overloaded at 09:11 passed through and did. registered2nd was not at its limit then (0% 04:05, 36% 14:19, 74% 19:26; no usage refusal); both accounts got an early weekly reset around 23:07.

SW310 (9d4db67e): only usage_limit_reached passes an account over; capacity 429s reach Codex unchanged on the websocket and HTTP paths and do not hold the account; a turn tries each account once and skips accounts at their limit.

SW311 (67d34ad8): both auth.json files are holders of whichever account they name; newer logins are filed with their cards before each request, each reconcile pass and any overwrite; renewals write through to each holder; proactive renewal at 7 days; a refused account clears from a newer WSL login. DECISION_LOG 2026-10-26 entry.
1.0.46 released (ec8f9fdf, eeeacd5b; public f630ee17; DMG run 40289262737).

SW312 (4b7f7f8e): sign_in_start / sign_in_finish / sign_in_status. Switchy builds the OAuth link (Codex parameters from openai/codex rust-v0.164.0, Claude's from the Claude Code 2.1.310 bundle), listens on 127.0.0.1:1455/1457 for Codex's callback, exchanges the code through the card's proxy, refuses a login of another account, files it with the card and clears its signed-out state; live auth files untouched. DECISION_LOG 2026-10-26 entry; README recipe.

First live use: user-b.zhang signed in from AdsPower 12 (exit 108.235.194.164 verified, email on the chooser and consent page) while Codex stayed on registered2nd; status done, identity valid, Pro, new week at 3% resetting 2026-11-02.

1.0.47 released (d73b1d20, 3524690c; public 68a680eb; DMG run 40335306641) and installed on the workstation. The switchy_account_signin skill uses the sign-in routes (four copies identical; dotfiles commits 30220cc70 Windows, 502e1b4d WSL). Worker briefs SW310-SW312 in brief_archive/.

Findings recorded, not acted on (no fix directed): (1) save_login_of_serving_account rewrites the auth files only when Windows' file holds another account, so WSL can stay on a different account; (2) 'recovered' switches mean 'another account's weekly window resets sooner', and a 15-minute reset difference moved traffic about every 5 min at the 99% threshold; the user questioned the label; (3) quota readings for a serving account had multi-hour gaps (none 04:05-14:19 and after 19:26 on 2026-10-25 while it served); (4) a continuing turn refused for usage when every account is at its limit costs one extra reconnect; (5) polling sign_in_status refreshes the tray on every call; (6) README Official providers still describes only the CLI sign-in.
session.latest_summary: 1.0.46 fixes capacity 429s bouncing between Codex accounts and keeps Codex logins renewed in WSL; 1.0.47 signs an account in without switching; user-b.zhang signed back in.

current_focus.summary: Switchy 1.0.47 is released (GitHub Latest, Windows installers and Apple Silicon DMG) and runs on the workstation. 1.0.46: a 429 'Codex is at capacity' goes back to Codex instead of moving the request between accounts, and a Codex login renewed in WSL is kept with its account (Switchy renews at 7 days; both auth.json files are read for every account). 1.0.47: sign_in_start / sign_in_finish / sign_in_status sign a Codex or Claude account in without switching; Switchy makes the code exchange through the card's own proxy (README 'Signing an account in without switching'; the switchy_account_signin skill uses it). user-b.zhang (f7649e3f) was signed back in that way from AdsPower 12 and is valid. The laptop has 1.0.40 with Switchy quit; another user's PC and Mac have 1.0.39. Await the user's feedback; the confirmations below stay pending under their triggers.

next_actions.summary: CONFIRM THE CRASH RESTART ON THE NEXT REAL CRASH (1.0.40). After any Switchy crash on the workstation: Application log event 1000 for switchy.exe, then within about a minute a new switchy.log starting with '[crash_restart] Windows will restart Switchy after a crash or hang' and the proxy on 15721 without a manual start; switchy.prev.log ends at the crash; ~/.switchy/crash.log gains an [ABNORMAL EXIT] entry naming the exception, any 'Windows ran out of memory' line and the dump path. A restart that did not happen while commit was still exhausted is the known single-attempt limit (finding doc option 2 is the backstop).

Confirm account-proxy coverage on the next natural Claude sign-in or renewal while Owen is selected, without forcing a new login. Claude Code's own exchange should log '[connect_tunnel] platform.claude.com:443 via socks5://82.26.163.142:45001'. For Switchy's renewal, observe '[claude_pool] refreshing login for provider=98e00f12...' and the successful refreshed-login message; the enforced per-account client route is owned by proxy/http_client.rs. Windows/WSL HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY, UK exit probes and telemetry tunnels were verified; a live sign-in/renewal using this route remains unobserved. Connection failures must stop rather than fall back to direct; country observations only warn.

CONFIRM THE RESTART PATH ON STEPHEN'S NEXT WINDOWS RESTART (1.0.29). In C:/Users/Administrator/.switchy/logs/switchy.prev.log after 'Session ending; handing the live configs back': '[session-end] claude/codex/gemini handed back', '[session-end] ... in WSL handed back', then 'Live configs handed back for the session end'. 'did not finish in 4 seconds' with the last [session-end] line shows which step stalls (Windows step = database lock, WSL step = WSL I/O); fix that step. In switchy.log: Switchy started within seconds of login (window hidden, launched with --autostart from HKCU Run), '[auto_launch] start at login on', proxy on 15721, and Claude Code / Codex answer without ECONNREFUSED.

CONFIRM CLAUDE LOGINS STAY IN STEP WITH WSL (1.0.27). In switchy.log, when an account WSL is signed in to renews: '[claude_pool] provider=... took the newer login from WSL' or 'wrote the refreshed login through to WSL', and no new 'invalid_grant' 'Refresh token not found or invalid' in account_switches/provider_health. WSL's ~/.claude/.credentials.json and ~/.switchy/accounts/<id>/credentials.json for that account should carry the same refreshToken after each renewal. CODEX TOO (1.0.46, SW311): when a Codex login renews, switchy.log shows either Switchy's own renewal once the login is 7 days old ('[codex_pool] refreshing login for provider=...' then 'login refreshed', and the refreshed login written through to each auth.json holding that account) or '[codex_pool] provider=... took the newer login from' WSL's auth.json; no Codex card is signed out with 'refresh token has already been used'.

CONFIRM ROTATION AND CODEX FAILOVER ON LIVE TRAFFIC (1.0.25/1.0.26). In C:/Users/Administrator/.switchy/logs/switchy.log and the switchy.db account_switches table: (a) when an account's five-hour window resets while another serves, a switch back to it with reason 'recovered' and detail "Another account's weekly limit resets sooner"; (b) a Codex turn refused for usage that continues an earlier one logs '[CodexWS] provider=... websocket closed (turn refused for usage; Codex resends it in full)' and the turn then completes on the next account with no error in Codex. GET http://127.0.0.1:15721/switchy/accounts shows current account, pool order, quota and atLimit per account. (c) 1.0.46 (SW310): a 429 'Codex is at capacity' (turn_rate_limit_exceeded) reaches the Codex terminal, account_switches gets no 'limit' row for it, the account is not held at its limit, and a turn never bounces between accounts (no runs of switches seconds apart).

VERIFY LOCAL PROXY OFF WITH AN OPEN CODEX WINDOW. the user was asked to turn Local proxy off in Settings > Pool, then use a Codex window opened while the proxy was on. Confirm in C:/Users/Administrator/.switchy/logs/switchy.log that "Proxy turned off; its listener stays up..." was logged, that the Codex window's later [Codex] requests still reached the proxy and answered, that netstat shows 127.0.0.1:15721 still LISTENING, and that Settings shows the proxy as off. Turning it back on must reuse the listener.

QUIT CASE WAITS ON STEPHEN. Quitting Switchy still breaks Codex windows opened under the proxy. He was offered a warning on quit naming the open Codex windows (small) or running the proxy as a process that outlives Switchy's window (large); he has not chosen. Build nothing until he does.
If the user directs request logging to be enabled, first make the Usage page's Turn on button apply to the running proxy, then enable it for Claude, Codex, and Gemini.

CONFIRM CURSOR/ANTIGRAVITY ON THE NEXT REAL SIGN-IN (1.0.43). No sign-in was run to test, and only one account of each exists. When the user adds a second account: enable the new empty card, open a NEW PowerShell, sign in. Expect: cursor-agent login prints 'Open a browser and navigate to this link' and opens no browser (user env NO_OPEN_BROWSER=1); agy started signed out shows its link with a code field and opens no browser (the profile function from ~/.switchy/manual_sign_in/agy_sign_in.ps1 sets SSH_CLIENT only when cmdkey lists no gemini:antigravity entry). Then switch back to the first card: switchy.log shows no '[cursor_account]'/'[antigravity_account] live login (...) is not the account' refusal for a normal switch, cursor-agent status and agy's log name the first account, and each card keeps its own email and usage badge ('[...] usage of provider=... N windows' lines). Kimi Code still opens the default browser (README limitation).

CONFIRM PLAN ACCOUNTS AND BALANCE MONITORS ON THE FIRST REAL KEY (1.0.45, SW309). Nothing was subscribed; plan quota, balance and Used in were checked only with fake keys (clean authentication failures from Z.ai and DeepSeek; Used in OpenCode wrote and removed its provider). When the user adds a real account (company page > Add account, or the README recipe over POST /switchy/invoke): choosing Claude Code switches Claude Code to a provider named '<Company> Â· <account>' whose env carries the key and the plan's host, and Claude Code answers on the plan's models; the card shows the plan's windows (Z.ai and MiniMax 5-hour and weekly, Kimi 5-hour, weekly and monthly, Command Code month's credits plus 5-hour and weekly when window-limited, OpenCode Go 5-hour, weekly and monthly); a DeepSeek, Moonshot or StepFun monitor shows the balance, and spend after a second reading. 'Unexpected balance response' or a parse error means the call's format differs from the documented one.
